newsitem.title: USA: Huizenga seen pressed to revise terms on ADT deal.
newsitem.headline: Huizenga seen pressed to revise terms on ADT deal.

text.p: More than two months after his Republic Industries Inc announced plans to buy ADT Ltd for $5 billion, aggressive businessman Wayne Huizenga is soon expected to revise the terms.
Industry sources expect Huizenga to offer ADT shareholders some measure of protection against a steep decline in the value of the deal.
The proposed deal is now worth $3.6 billion due to a sharp decline in Republic stock. It is also being opposed by Western Resources Inc, which holds 24.3 percent of ADT.

"The ball is really in Republic's court as to how far it will go to guarantee ADT stockholders the price that they want. This is strategically an important deal for Republic," said analyst Jeffrey Kessler of Lehman Brothers.
Republic first announced plans on July 1 to acquire ADT in a stock transaction valued at $5 billion.
But the deal soon ran into stumbling blocks as Republic's stock price sank below $19 per share. The terms of the transaction were based on a Republic stock price of $26.
Since then, the two companies have reportedly been haggling over new terms for the deal.
Republic has confirmed that negotiations were ongoing, but has declined to specify the nature of the talks. ADT has previously declined to comment on the negotiations.

The transaction has generated concern on Wall Street because the companies have not filed a shareholder proxy with the U.S. Securities and Exchnage Commission and financial advisor Merrill Lynch has not issued a fairness opinion on the transaction.
"The deal is really in limbo right now," said one Wall Street takeover stock trader.
Huizenga, the powerful executive who built Blockbuster Entertainment and now owns three Florida professional sports teams, is reportedly eager to push the deal forward.

Sources familiar with the companies said Huizenga this week told investors he wants to file the documents by next week. A Republic spokesman did not confirm that timetable, saying it was expected to be filed in several weeks.

Western disclosed its opposition in a September 13 federal filing and a spokeswoman on Thursday confirmed its position. Although it has not divulged its strategy, Western has won government approval to buy up to 50 percent of ADT shares.
The Kansas utility, which has said it was not consulted about the transaction, has long been considered a spoiler.

"The real question is, can (Western) really do anything about (the transaction)? That is still unclear. I'm somewhat skeptical about their ability to block it," said analyst Andrew Jeffrey of Robertson Stephens & Co.
ADT could not be reached for comment and a Republic spokesman declined to comment on Western's opposition.

An acquisition of ADT is considered a huge strategic step for Republic, which has bought 19 security businesses since entering the industry about a year ago. Its two other major areas of business are solid waste and used cars.
